title: The IARC perspective on alcohol reduction or cessation and cancer risk
authors: Gapstur SM, Bouvard V, Nethan ST, Freudenheim JL, Abnet CC, English DR, et al.
population: IARC Handbooks of Cancer Prevention Working Group on alcohol reduction or cessation
funder: Supported by the French National Cancer Institute (INCa/IReSP 16650) and by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (NOFO number, CDC-RFA-DP22-2208).
authorConflicts: Working Group members provided Declarations of Interest; on review by the IARC, none was considered to represent a potential or significant conflict of interest.
result: Sufficient evidence that alcohol reduction or cessation reduces the risk of oral and oesophageal cancer; limited evidence for laryngeal, colorectal and breast cancer; sufficient mechanistic evidence that alcohol cessation reduces alcohol-related carcinogenesis. An estimated 741,300 new cancer cases worldwide in 2020 (4.1% of all new cases) were attributable to alcohol consumption.
